plain_summary: Check lithium follow-up after a systemic NSAID is started during lithium treatment.

medicine_groups.name: Lithium
medicine_groups.note: Count systemic lithium, including a supply labelled simply lithium.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Use systemic preparations, including systemic COX-2 inhibitors. Count aspirin only when the directions show an anti-inflammatory regimen. Exclude skin and eye preparations. Check the form on shared brands such as Voltaren, Feldene and Orudis. Gels and eye drops do not count. Check aspirin directions and purpose even for dispersible tablets. An antiplatelet regimen does not count. Nuromol, Maxigesic and Combigesic contain ibuprofen with paracetamol. Nurofen Plus contains ibuprofen with codeine. Vimovo contains naproxen with esomeprazole.

rule_for_models: After 90 observable NSAID-free days, count a new systemic NSAID during lithium treatment as day zero. Exclude low-dose antiplatelet aspirin and non-systemic use. If exposure is unclear, ask about the purpose, daily dose, actual start and whether lithium continued. Report at most a possible gap. Check for a lithium level on days 5 to 7 even after a lithium dose reduction, or use the individual deadline for this start. A level on day 7 counts. Give no finding when follow-up is complete. A later level closes an outstanding test request if it documents follow-up for this exposure. Check any further test due under the plan. If follow-up is not yet due, give no finding. Once day 7 or the planned deadline is reached without the expected follow-up, report only a possible gap. Cite the lithium supply covering the start, new NSAID, any baseline result used and the supply or observed dose showing lithium treatment through the deadline. Ask about outside testing and new tremor, unsteadiness or vomiting since the start.
cannot_be_seen: Outside pathology or follow-up may be missing. An incomplete observation window cannot establish an overdue test.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm whether a serum lithium level was checked around days 5 to 7 after the systemic NSAID was started, or whether an individual monitoring plan was arranged?

needs_facts.meets: Use the lithium level in mmol/L and its sample date for this NSAID course. If only the date of the follow-up level is known, enter “test performed” with that date. A baseline or undated result cannot establish follow-up. Check the individual due date if there is one.

needs_facts.what: Lithium follow-up for this NSAID start
needs_facts.meets: At the date under review, check the plan for this NSAID start. A documented plan covers the interval until its test is due. Once due, check whether that test was taken. With no plan use days 5 to 7. If a plan or its completion is uncertain and follow-up is due, keep a possible gap open and ask for the dates.

options.words: The planned test is due and has not been done
No plan and no follow-up level by day 7
Follow-up is not yet due for this NSAID start
Follow-up was done for this start and no further test is due
